tldr: This thread is a broad reading list on LLM behavior, reliability and knowledge. Oct 16-28 papers covered sycophancy, hallucination, steering and evals, then Mistral Large 4 landed on Hugging Face and vLLM on Oct 29 as work shifted to memory and retrieval.
whats_new: Nov 5: the FedReason preprint tests an LLM as a weight-space aggregator for heterogeneous federated learning, alongside Anthropic's zkSNARK provable-inference work and the Show HN tool Thinker.
why_it_matters: The practical thread is context cost and knowledge handling: retrieval, memory and context trimming decide agent reliability and token spend more than any single model release here.

beats.headline: Early papers probe sycophancy, code-translation hallucination and search-state awareness
Price comparison, spectral edits, low-resource adaptation and KG-to-text benchmarks
Long-horizon search evals, neuron steering, vulnerability probing, continual learning and translated benchmarks
Mistral Large 4 ships on Hugging Face and vLLM; papers turn to self-learning and memory
Knowledge integration, retrieval harnesses, text-to-SQL, pruning and retrieval-to-parametric memory
Provable inference, context engines, answerability judgments, federated aggregation and a token-saving tool

open_questions: Do compiled-knowledge and parametric-memory methods beat plain retrieval on production agent workloads?
Will provable inference become practical for hosted model APIs?
Do Mistral Large 4 serving claims on vLLM hold up in independent benchmarks?
take_for_builders: If agent token limits bite, measure context trimming and caching against your own eval set before adopting it; treat the preprints and the Show HN tool as unreplicated.
